subject: Renewal: support uplift + latency SLOs and capacity expansion
messages:
From: Ethan Brooks <ethan@nodaltech.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@nodaltech.com
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — premium SLA + burst capacity

Hi Soojin,

Our contract with Redwood comes up for renewal in late October and the team wants to discuss a support uplift and committed capacity increase. We've been seeing periodic tail latency spikes during end-of-month processing; we want to lock in a 99.9% p50/p95 latency target for our critical routes and a burst pool for 2x our baseline TPS during invoice runs.

High-level asks:
- Premium SLA addendum (latency SLOs for two routes: /generate and /embed)
- Reserved burst capacity and a way to guarantee priority scheduling during spikes
- Pricing/credits for committed capacity + how overage will be billed

Can you send a proposed mutual action plan and any SLA language you’d expect to add? We’d like to loop legal early (cc’d contracts@nodaltech.com).

Thanks,
Ethan Brooks
Head of Platform — NodalTech

[Attachment: usage_snapshot_Aug2028.csv]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan@nodaltech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — premium SLA + burst capacity

Ethan — thanks for the note and for looping legal. Glad to hear you want to formalize latency guarantees and burst capacity. I've attached a first-pass mutual action plan and our standard SLA addendum for premium support so you and your contracts team can review.

What we'll need from you to make a tight proposal:
- Typical and peak TPS (30/60/90 day windows) for /generate and /embed
- Example windows where you see the end-of-month spikes (UTC ranges)
- Any retention or audit log retention requirements tied to support incident reviews

Quick summary of what we're proposing internally:
- Premium SLA addendum: target latency commitments (p50/p95) per route + uptime guarantee; financial credits for SLA misses capped to the renewal term
- Reserved burst pool: dedicated GPU capacity reservable up to 2.0x baseline for 4-hour windows; higher priority routing during bursts
- Support tier: move to Premium Care (24/7 triage, named TAM, monthly SLO reviews)
- Pricing: blended model (monthly committed capacity + per-token overage for bursts) with a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration cost

I've attached: NodalTech_MutualActionPlan_v2.docx and SLA_Addendum_v3.pdf.

Propose we schedule a 30-min call next week to walk through numbers and owner alignment (marissa will lead onboarding, ben will handle commercial). Available slots: Tue 9/19 10:00–11:30 PT, Wed 9/20 13:00–15:00 PT.

Best,
Soji n Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Sep 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: NodalTech renewal — latency SLOs and burst capacity (internal)

Internal — forwarding Nodal's procurement questions so we can prep for Wed's sync. Short asks below; copying context above. Please reply-all with recommended wording and a quick cost example.

Priya asked:
- Measurement window & metric collectors for SLA credits (we typically use per-route p95 measured at the edge and collected by our telemetry with a 1-week rolling window). Thoughts on making this deterministic for finance?
- Termination/scaling down committed capacity mid-term — our standard is a 30-day notice and pro-rated refunds for commitments not consumed; is that safe or do we need to carve exceptions for burst reservations?
- Billing model for burst pool — is it reserved (monthly) vs used (metered)? She wants simple invoice examples for three scenarios (low, normal, end-of-month peak).

Aditya — can you run a brief model: baseline 800 TPS /generate, 300 TPS /embed average; end-of-month peaks to 2200 combined for 3–6 hours. Provide two cost examples: (A) make burst pool 2.0x reserved capacity (monthly commit) (B) keep burst metered, paid only when used.
Ben — can you draft proposed deterministic SLA language for credit calc and the termination clause we can provide to Priya? Keep finance-friendly wording.

Really tight turnaround — aim for internal responses by EOD today so we can send a consolidated reply to Priya tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
So j in

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan@nodaltech.com>, Priya Singh <priya@nodaltech.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Sep 2028 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — premium SLA + burst capacity — proposed terms

Ethan / Priya — appreciate the quick turn. Below is the consolidated response and the next steps. Attaching a redline-ready mutual action plan and a sample invoice with three burst scenarios.

Short answers to your procurement questions:
1) SLA measurement & credits:
   - Measurement: per-route latency (p50/p95) computed at our edge telemetry, aggregated in 1-minute buckets and evaluated on a 7-day rolling lookback to determine SLA status. This approach provides deterministic, auditable windows for finance.
   - Credits: SLA credits are applied monthly and capped at 3 months of monthly fees per 12-month term; credits are issued as invoice deductions. Wording in the attached SLA_Addendum_v3.pdf reflects this.
2) Termination / scaling down commitments:
   - We permit committed capacity reductions once per 12-month term with 30 days' notice; any unused portion of the commitment is pro-rated and applied as account credits. Burst reservations (if reserved) are billed monthly and treated as separate line items; reductions to reserved burst pools require 60 days' notice to avoid capacity reallocation churn.
3) Burst pool billing and priority:
   - Option A (Reserved Burst): customer reserves a burst pool sized to 2.0x baseline; billed monthly as a committed line item. Reserved bursts are prioritized in routing and guaranteed for configured windows up to 4 hours per event.
   - Option B (Metered Burst): customer pays only for used burst capacity at a higher per-token rate; reserved routing priority not guaranteed but we provide aggressive soft-priority during events.

Attached: NodalTech_MutualActionPlan_v2.docx (redline-enabled) and sample-invoice-burst-scenarios.xlsx. Also here's a DocuSign link to the mutual action plan for convenience: https://docusign.com/rooms/abc123-NOD-2028-004

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether Nodal prefers Option A (reserved) or Option B (metered) by end of day Thu 9/21.
- Once we confirm, we'll circulate a single redline for legal to approve and target signature within two weeks.
- Marissa will schedule a 60-min technical onboarding in week of Oct 2 if we proceed with reserved burst.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
